title: The Green Stars of Oakhaven
story:
Apothecary Lane was rich with the heavy, sleepy scents of crushed lavender and dried chamomile. To James, the herbal air felt like a quiet blanket after the shouting of the market square. Here, the damp cobblestones muffled his footsteps, and the narrow walls kept the wind at bay. He walked slowly, letting his fingers brush against the rough brick walls of the shops.

He had known the wet, tangled green of the Great Canopy. He had known the hot, dry dust of the Whispering Flats. Now, he was learning the cold, patient stone of the human town. He paused before a dark shop window, watching his reflection ripple across the glass. The brass canister on his shoulder caught a stray glint of light, reminding him of ticking clocks, warm hearths, and the gentle old man who had given him a map.

A sudden wave of weariness washed over him, but he did not want to sleep here in the narrow dark. He wanted to go back to a place of promise. Navigating by the memory of the canal's mist, James made his way back through the quietening streets until the massive, domed silhouette of the Grand Library rose before him against the twilight sky.

He climbed the monumental stone steps, his small shadow stretching long behind him. Finding a dry, sheltered alcove beside the grand wooden doors, James curled up and pulled his green sea-glass from his pocket. Through the emerald pane, he watched the first gas lamps of Oakhaven flicker to life, turning the misty street below into a quiet constellation of green stars.
location: A sheltered stone alcove on the steps of the Grand Library
